step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified all 8 nodes depicted in the architecture diagram: two mobile actors (Melco Club Mobile App, WeChat Mobile App), API Gateway, Lambda Authorizer, Lambda Services, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, and Third Parties.
2. Standardized node service names against the valid vocabulary list.
3. Segmented workflows into two distinct logical flows: Flow 0 for incoming app traffic and authentication via Lambda Authorizer, and Flow 1 for microservice business logic execution calling DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, and external Third Parties.
4. Formatted output strictly into JSON schema with no raw control characters inside strings.

graph.name: Melco Resorts Serverless Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless backend architecture powering Melco Club applications across iOS/Android and WeChat platforms.

nodes.name: MELCO CLUB MOBILE APP
nodes.notes: iOS/Android app targeted at international customers.

nodes.name: WECHAT MOBILE APP
nodes.notes: WeChat mini-app targeted at mainland China market.

nodes.name: API GW
nodes.notes: Entry endpoint receiving HTTPS requests from both mobile apps.

nodes.name: AUTHORIZER
nodes.notes: Lambda authorizer function that decodes and validates tokens.

nodes.name: SERVICES
nodes.notes: Separate microservice Lambda functions handling business capabilities like hotel and dining reservations.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.notes: Fully managed NoSQL database with individual table scaling.

nodes.name: SECRETS MANAGER
nodes.notes: Manages credential lifecycle for third-party integrations.

edges.notes: Melco Club Mobile App sends requests to API Gateway.
WeChat Mobile App sends requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes Lambda Authorizer for authentication.
API Gateway routes authorized requests to Lambda Services.
Lambda Services reads/writes persistent data to DynamoDB.
Lambda Services fetches third-party credentials from Secrets Manager.
Lambda Services interacts with external Third Party APIs.
